key_insight: Multiplicative noise is necessary to recover the expected gamma distribution of equilibrium temperature fluctuations, including nonzero skewness and excess kurtosis that additive noise misses.
engineering_relevance: Accurate higher-order fluctuation statistics matter when predicting nonlinear functions of hydrodynamic fields in mesoscopic fluid simulations.
method: Analyze second-, third-, and fourth-order central moments in finite-volume stochastic heat-equation discretizations.
Derive persistent modeling errors and improve Dirichlet boundary treatment.
Assess Stratonovich-based time integrators and test full compressible stochastic Navier–Stokes simulations.
evidence_signal: Analytical results and numerical simulations identify higher-moment errors, show that the improved boundary formulation eliminates large boundary-adjacent third-moment errors, and support applicability beyond the heat equation.
watch_item: Reducing the time step alone does not eliminate inherent modeling errors; noise interpretation, boundary treatment, and integrator choice remain important.
paper_title: Variance and Higher-Order Moments in Computational Fluctuating Hydrodynamics with Multiplicative Noise
